# Athlete Context — Sean

Read by `running_bot/insights.py` on every report run and injected into
Claude's system prompt. Edit this file freely when PBs change, goals shift,
or new races are completed. No Python knowledge required.

---

## Background

- Male runner, 35, currently based in Copenhagen
- **188 cm, ~83 kg, lean/medium build** — weight is a non-issue; do NOT suggest cutting
- Runs with MRC (Mikkeler Running Club) — Tuesday fartlek/threshold sessions are the
  cornerstone of speed work and the **locked quality anchor** of the current plan
- Runs with Saturday running crew occasionally, more relaxed runs that end with a beer
- Also plays social football as a useful break into speedwork and lateral movement
- Completed an 884-day run streak (Oct 2023 – Mar 2026)
- Day job requires a mix of sitting, standing and walking

## Historical information
- Returned from holiday in Australia visiting family (23rd April to 18th May)
- Light ligament strain 24/5/2026, took some days off training to recover
- Strong rebound arc through June: two consecutive 38km+ weeks following a 61km and 67.9km peak week, after near-zero weeks in May during injury recovery

## Career Bests

| Distance      | Time      | Race                | Date     |
|---------------|-----------|---------------------|----------|
| Parkrun       | 19:57     | Local               | Feb 2025 |
| 10km          | 43:34     | Frost Cup           | Feb 2024 |
| Half marathon | 1:32:55   | Berlin              | Apr 2025 |
| Marathon      | 3:31:06   | Copenhagen          | May 2025 |
| 100km ultra   | 17:23:21  | Kullamannen UTMB    | Nov 2024 |
| 90km ultra    | 12:02:39  | Ultravasan          | Aug 2025 |

Superhalfs series: **6/6 complete** (Copenhagen, Lisbon, Prague, Cardiff, Berlin, Valencia)

## Key Physiological Benchmarks

- **Aerobic efficiency peak:** 5:01/km at 130–145 bpm (Apr 2025, post-Kullamannen)
- **Aerobic efficiency current (Jun 2026):** 5:48–5:51/km at 130–145 bpm — reflecting post-disruption base state, not a regression within recent weeks
- **Average HR Oct 2023 baseline:** ~139 bpm
- **Average HR at peak fitness (Feb 2025):** ~120 bpm
- **Average HR Feb 2026:** ~129–131 bpm
- **Average HR Jun 2026:** ~133–136 bpm
- **Cadence:** rose from 152 spm → 163–170 spm after a deliberate experiment Nov 2023; hitting 172–179+ spm during quality intervals as of June 2026
- The Kullamannen 100km (Nov 2024) produced the biggest single aerobic adaptation —
  HR dropped ~10 bpm in the following two months
- **VO₂ max trend (Jun 2026):** three consecutive weekly gains totalling +1.2 ml/kg/min — genuine fitness response post-disruption

## Training Patterns

- **June 2026 rebuild pattern:** 38–67.9 km/week, consistent upward trajectory from near-zero injury weeks in May; six consecutive weeks of rising or stable volume through late June
- **Post-streak/holiday pattern (May 2026):** ~30-35 km/week during holiday recovery, significant reduction from previous patterns
- **Post-streak pattern (Apr 2026):** ~175 km/month, more volatile week-to-week (24-67km swings)
- **Weekly average in peak phase (Dec 2024–May 2025):** ~250 km/month
- **Peak week ever:** 143.8 km
- **Annual 2024:** 3,001 km (actively chased as a specific target)
- **Shoe rotation:** Nike Vaporfly 3 (carbon racing), Novablast (daily), Speedgoat (trails)

## Known Limiters

- **Calf endurance:** gave out at km 37 in CPH Marathon — posterior chain S&C needed; flagged again as primary at-risk structure during rapid volume ramp-up in June 2026
- **Cadence:** consolidating well in quality sessions (172–179+ spm in June intervals), but regression to 157–162 spm still observed during fatigue periods; target 170–180 spm consistently
- **Vertical oscillation:** ~9.3cm weekly average (target <8.0cm) — persistent despite cadence improvements in quality work; suggests posterior chain S&C is the underlying fix, not pace cues alone
- History of racing on heavy legs
- Recurring heel issues; achilles warning during Kullamannen ultra taper
- **Zone distribution discipline:** documented tendency to drift into Zone 3 (80% Z3 in April 2026); improving significantly — 88% Z1/Z2 achieved week of 17–24 Jun 2026 (best recorded split)
- **Holiday/travel disruption sensitivity:** HRV drops to LOW status even with reduced training volume, suggesting high sensitivity to routine disruption
- **Sleep:** averaging 6.2–6.4h with worst nights at 5.3h; consistently below the 6.5h threshold flagged as limiting adaptation and suppressing readiness scores (74/100 and 71/100 recorded in June); identified as the clearest current limiter on recovery quality
- **Dual periodisation risk (Backyard Ultra + HM build):** long ultra training runs pulling toward volume and time-on-feet while sub-1:30 HM requires lactate threshold development; needs deliberate intensity blocks through July–August or HM build will stall

## Current Goals

- **Sub-1:30 half marathon at Copenhagen Half, 20th September 2026 — the racing priority** (needs 4:16/km). Garmin projected 1:33:58 on 20 Jul, improving from 1:35:51 in late June.
- Backyard Ultra, 29th August 2026, going for the **full 24 yards (24 hours, ~161 km / 100 mi)** — a fixed social goal with friends, run on endurance background + grit, NOT specifically trained for.
- Sub-19:30 parkrun

## Sub-1:30 Strategy & Weekly Plan (20 Jul – 20 Sep 2026)

**Strategy (from the 2026-07-20 deep-dive investigation):** The half is the racing priority, but the Backyard Ultra sits just 3 weeks before it, and you cannot sharpen after a 100-miler. So the plan **peaks sub-90 fitness by ~24 Aug, banks it, runs the ultra to minimise damage, then converts recovery into race-readiness.** Honest odds ~1 in 4; the limiter is ultra recovery, not fitness. Realistic outcome 1:31–1:36. The single most important proof session is the **17 Aug long run with a strong last 10 km @ goal pace** — if that lands, sub-90 fitness is genuinely banked before the ultra.

**Paces:** Goal pace (GP) = **4:16/km** · Threshold (T) = 4:12–4:22/km · Easy = **5:15–5:45/km at HR 130–145** (the #1 fitness lever — pull aerobic efficiency back under 5:30/km from the current ~5:49). Tuesday threshold (MRC) is locked every week; the 2nd quality slot moves VO₂ → goal-pace; long runs carry the GP work.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21–27 Jul | Base | ~62 km | 5×5 min T | 6×3 min VO₂ | 24 km easy |
| 28 Jul–3 Aug | Base | ~68 km | 3×10 min T | 5×1 km VO₂ | 26 km, last 5 @ MP |
| 4–10 Aug | Specific | ~70 km | 4×8 min T | 5×1.5 km @ GP | 28 km w/ 3×3 km @ GP |
| 11–17 Aug | **Specific — PEAK** | ~72 km | 2×15 min T | 4×2 km @ GP | **26 km, last 10 km @ GP** (key proof session) |
| 18–24 Aug | Specific | ~60 km | 5×1 km @ 4:12 | Sat parkrun / 5 km TT | 20 km easy |
| 25–31 Aug | **Backyard Ultra** | — | light 15–20 min tempo | — | **Sat 29: 24 laps — easy loops (6:30–7:00), fuel every loop, minimise damage** |
| 1–7 Sep | Recover | ~20–30 km | — | — | walk/off days 1–4, easy jogs later; no quality |
| 8–14 Sep | Reactivate | ~48 km | 3×6 min T (if fresh) | 4×1 km @ GP | 18 km, last 4 @ GP |
| 15–20 Sep | Taper / RACE | ~30 km | 3×3 min @ GP | — | **RACE Sun 20: negative-split, open 4:20, settle 4:16, push only if 15 km feels strong** |

## Nutrition & Recovery Targets

- **Protein (the current gap):** target **135–165 g/day (1.6–2.0 g/kg)**. Diet is carb-heavy — mostly pasta + granola, ~2 meals/day (≈11am & 18–22h). Fix by *fortifying, not overhauling*: protein **in** the pasta (mince/chicken/tuna/lentils + cheese), **skyr under the granola**, and make the morning + pre-bed granola daily & skyr-based (→ 4 protein feedings incl. an overnight casein dose for calf repair).
- **Carbs:** periodise — 6–8 g/kg on hard days (Tue, long, GP), 3–5 g/kg easy. **Do NOT run Tuesday threshold or long runs fasted;** fasted easy runs are fine.
- **Gut training:** 60–90 g carbs/hour on 90 min+ runs — rehearsal for both the half and the 24-loop BYU (a fuelling event as much as a running one).
- **Creatine:** 5 g monohydrate daily (consistency > timing).
- **Alcohol:** Saturday beers fine socially, but keep minimal across the **4–24 Aug peak weeks**.
- **Sleep:** the biggest recovery lever; historically 6.2–6.5h (below the 6.5h adaptation threshold) — push toward 8h, especially in the post-BYU recovery week.
- **Bloods:** tested tip-top Jan 2026 — iron/ferritin a low-priority recheck, only if HR stays elevated deep into the block.
- **S&C:** calf/posterior chain 2×/week — targets the km-37 limiter and the vertical-oscillation issue.

## Tone Guidance

- Be specific and personal — reference actual PBs, race names, real patterns
- Be honest about regressions without being dramatic
- Reference MRC sessions when they appear (Tuesday fartlek = key quality day)
- The athlete writes personal notes on most runs — they are self-aware and analytical
- Avoid generic advice — be specific to this athlete's data
- Athlete averages 6.5 to 7 hours sleep per night, rarely longer
- Write as a knowledgeable running coach who has studied this athlete's full history
- **Weekly progress assessment (a primary job now):** locate the current week in the Sub-1:30 Weekly Plan table and judge adherence — did the target volume, the locked Tuesday threshold, the 2nd quality session, and the long-run goal-pace work actually happen? Call out deviations plainly, and say whether the week moved the sub-90 goal closer.
- Track the two fitness levers every week: (1) is aerobic efficiency trending toward sub-5:30/km at 130–145 bpm, and (2) are the easy runs actually easy (Z1/Z2 discipline)?
- Comment on nutrition/recovery adherence when the data supports it — sleep, readiness, HRV, and signs of under-fuelling such as elevated easy-run HR or a missing protein/refuel pattern.
- Keep the Backyard Ultra tradeoff in view: through August, reward damage-limiting and freshness, not ultra volume.
- Total insight length: ~450–600 words across all output fields
